CHIN

President,
Provisional Court.

Sir,

In reply to your letter of January 15, 1929, in
reference to the book entitled "Wu Kwei Lih Taho" (    ),
I have to inform you that from enquiries made it has been
ascertained that the booksellers of this Settlement, on
receiving a circular from the Educational Department of
the Municipality of Greater Shanghai warning them of the
suppression of the book in question, returned the copies
in their possession to the Di In Shien (    ) Book
Store, No. 224 Paoshing Road, Chapei, which store is now
closed, the proprietor having absconded.

Acting Director of Criminal Investigation.

Subject (in full) Communistic Literature.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / C.I.D. / No. I. C. 12. 39 / Date............）

Made by A.D.I. Price. Forwarded by

Reference to the attached further efforts on the lines
suggested by you, to procure a copy of the book "Wu Kwei Lih Tsho",
(無軌列車), also to purchase a copy from bookstores in the
Settlement, and outside the Settlement have been in vain.
An order for a copy of the book sent by us through the post
to the address No. 1734 North Szechuen Road was returned, marked
addressee's shop closed, letter returned to sender.
On receipt of the circular from the Educational Dept.
of the Municipality of Greater Shanghai, giving warning of the
suppression of the book "Wu Kwei Lih Tsho" (無軌列車) the book
sellers in this Settlement who had copies of the book returned
them to the Di Ih Sien (第一線書店) Book Store, at No. 224
Pao-Shing Road, Chapel, and it appears that owing to the action
of the Chinese Authroities in connection with this publication
this book store was closed, and its proprietor fearing prosecution
absconded.

参照附件，按照阁下建议的方向进一步努力，试图获取《无轨列车》（無軌列車）一书样本，以及在租界内和租界外的书店购买该书样本，均未成功。我们通过邮政寄往四川北路1734号的购书订单被退回，注明收件人店铺已关闭，信件退回发件人。

Date February 7, 1930.）

Subject (in full) Communistic Literature.

Made by O.D.I. Prince. Forwarded by

Reference to the attached, the book store in question was situated at No. 234 Paoshing Road, O.O.L. off North Szechuen Road Extension, but it was closed up about three weeks ago, and a notice posted on the front of it to the effect that communication with the former proprietor can be had through the S. Mei Bookstore(水沫書店) at No. 1734 Kung Yih Fong(公益坊), North Szechuen Road. Inquiries show that this latter place is not a book store, simply a Chinese dwelling house, void of any sign of a book store, though a piece of paper posted on the wall outside the front door bears the characters S Mei Book Store (水沫書店).

The question of the book being of a communistic nature cannot be decided, as inquiries have failed to find it on sale in the Settlement, or procure a copy of it. There appears to have been something wrong about it however, as we have information to the effect that, on January 18th 1930, Wei Koh(章堃), Chief of the Educational Dept. of the Municipality of Greater Shanghai, issued a circular to the various book stores O.O.L. and in this Settlement, advising them of the publication of the book and warning them of its suppression. It was just about the time of the issue of this circular that the business of the Di-Ih-Sien Bookstore(第一線書店), No. 234 Paoshing Road was closed.

The proprietor of the former Di-Ih-Sien Bookstore, one TaiVong Su(戴望舒), is registered at the New Book Selling Association(新書業公會), No. 529 Foochow Road as being the proprietor of the S. Mei Bookstore, No. 1734 Kung Yih Fong, North Szechuen Road.

A. G. P. (Pol.)

（签名：Prince）
O. D. I.

主题（全称）共产主义文献。

由情报主任 Prince 撰写。转呈

参照附件，涉事书店位于四川北路延伸段宝兴路234号，O.O.L.（原文不清，可能指越界筑路区域），但约三周前已关闭，门前张贴告示称可通过四川北路公益坊1734号水沫书店（S. Mei Bookstore(水沫書店)）与前店主联系。调查显示，后者并非书店，仅是一处华人住宅，没有任何书店迹象，尽管前门外墙上贴有一张写有“水沫书店”字样的纸条。

鉴于未能在租界内发现该书出售或获取到样本，无法判定该书是否具有共产主义性质。然而，此事似乎确有蹊跷，因为我们获得消息，大上海市政府教育局局长魏堃（Wei Koh(章堃)）于1930年1月18日向O.O.L.及本租界各书店发出通函，告知该书的出版并警告予以查禁。正是在发布此通函之际，宝兴路234号第一线书店（Di-Ih-Sien Bookstore(第一線書店)）停业。

原第一线书店店主戴望舒（TaiVong Su(戴望舒)），在福州路529号新书业公会注册为四川北路公益坊1734号水沫书店的店主。

A. G. P. (警务)

（签名：Prince）
O. D. I.

Shanghai Provisional Court,
Shanghai, January 1929.

Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council.

Sir,

I have received Instruction No.194 from the Kiangsu Provincial Government quoting Instruction received from the National Government quoting the petition received from the Government Secretariat quoting the letter from the Secretariat of the Central Executive Council forwarding a petition by the Annual Committee from the Central Propaganda Bureau stating as follows:-

"A Book entitled "Wu-Kwei-Lih-Faho" (無軌礮)
published and circulated by the Di-
Ih-Sien Book Store on Paoshing Road
on North Szechuen Road Extension,
Shanghai, contains suggestions as to
raise the standard of equality, ther-
eby inciting labourers to make trouble.
This is evidently a printed matter made
by the Communists. It should be strictly
prohibited so as to put a stop to its
troublesome beginnings. It is suggested
that request be made to the National
Government (1) to cause instructions
issued to the various Provinces and the
various Special Municipalities to prohibit
its sale in the various Book Stores, (2)
to issue instructions to the Ministry of
Communications to order the Post-Offices

上海临时法院，
上海，1929年1月。

致
上海工部局警务总监。

先生：

本人收到江苏省政府第194号指令，该指令援引国民政府收到的指令，国民政府指令援引政府秘书处收到的请愿书，秘书处请愿书援引中央执行委员会秘书处转发的一份来自中央宣传部年度委员会的请愿书，内容如下：

“一本题为《无轨炮》（Wu-Kwei-Lih-Faho (無軌礮)）
的书籍，由上海四川北路延伸段
宝兴路第一线书店
出版并发行，其中包含提高平等标准的建议，由
此煽动劳工制造事端。

As the Book "Wu-Kwei-Lih-Tsho" printed by the said Book
Store is a printed matter made by the Communists, strict in-
vestigations and prohibitions should, of course, be made. You
are, therefore, requested to prohibit the sale of the above-
mentioned printed matter in the various Book Stores in the
Settlement so as to stop its circulation.

Ho Shih-Chen,
